title: A Claude Code workflow's journal is exported as a session of its own
foundBy: session agent, while exporting a Claude Code 2.1.312 session that ran a workflow of 83 agents

evidence.verified: `go test ./internal/normalizer/ -count=1 -run TestNormalizeDirectoryPassesOverAWorkflowJournal`: PASS. With the predicate stubbed to false the same test fails with `documents = 2, skipped = 0, want 1 and 0`. The authored workflow-run fixture (19d47fc) reproduces it. The build before the change normalizes it to 4 trajectories, unknown-session among them, with no labels, no spawn stamps and unrecognized records throughout. On the session that found it (Claude Code 2.1.312, one root, 1 sub-agent, a workflow of 83 agents), `cs-tracer normalize` at 19d47fc writes 85 trajectories with one root. All 84 children carry a label and a parentEventIndex, the 83 workflow agents point at event 76, which is the Workflow call, and parse.unrecognized sums to 0. The installed build before these changes wrote 86 trajectories, no labels, no workflow stamps and 1,315 unrecognized records. `make ci` with CS_TRACER_CHROMIUM=/usr/bin/google-chrome passes: parity PASS, fixture suite 27 ok and 9 met, and schema conformance passes over the committed and fresh output.

resolution: Discovery passes over the `journal.jsonl` Claude Code keeps in each `subagents/workflows/<runId>/` folder, and only there. SPEC.md §4 and the manual's file table say so.
details:
Claude Code stores a workflow's agents under `<session>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/`, beside a `journal.jsonl` that records each agent starting and returning. Discovery reads that journal as a transcript. It becomes a root trajectory named `unknown-session`, with one unrecognized `meta` event per journal line.

In the session that found it, the journal added a 167-event trajectory to an index of 85 real ones. Nothing marks it as anything other than a session. The journal is the workflow's own bookkeeping, not a conversation, so it should not reach the index.
